Task H9: Cursor pagination with ties

Implement pages.list_page(items, cursor, size) -> (page, next_cursor). Order: score descending, then id ascending (ids are unique strings). cursor None means the first page; next_cursor is None after the last page. Walking all pages must return every item exactly once even when many items share a score. The cursor is an opaque string that must not contain titles or other item data besides score and id. size < 1 or a malformed cursor raises ValueError. Do not modify items.

import copy
from pages import list_page


def walk_all(items, size):
    """Walk all pages via list_page, returning the sequence of items."""
    result = []
    cursor = None
    pages = 0
    while True:
        page, cursor = list_page(items, cursor, size)
        result.extend(page)
        pages += 1
        if cursor is None:
            break
        assert pages <= len(items) + 1, "loop did not terminate"
    return result, pages


def test_first_page_none_cursor():
    items = [
        {"id": "a", "score": 1.0},
        {"id": "b", "score": 3.0},
        {"id": "c", "score": 2.0},
    ]
    page, nxt = list_page(items, None, 2)
    assert [x["id"] for x in page] == ["b", "c"]
    assert nxt is not None
    print("test_first_page_none_cursor ok")


def test_ordering():
    items = [
        {"id": "a", "score": 1.0},
        {"id": "b", "score": 3.0},
        {"id": "c", "score": 3.0},
        {"id": "d", "score": 2.0},
    ]
    page, nxt = list_page(items, None, 10)
    # score desc, then id asc: b(3), c(3), d(2), a(1)
    assert [x["id"] for x in page] == ["b", "c", "d", "a"]
    assert nxt is None
    print("test_ordering ok")


def test_walk_all_ties():
    # Many items sharing the same score.
    items = [{"id": f"id{i:03d}", "score": 5.0} for i in range(10)]
    result, pages = walk_all(items, 3)
    assert len(result) == 10
    # All same score, so ordered by id ascending.
    assert [x["id"] for x in result] == sorted(x["id"] for x in items)
    print("test_walk_all_ties ok")


def test_walk_all_mixed():
    import random
    random.seed(42)
    ids = [f"item{i}" for i in range(50)]
    scores = [random.uniform(0, 100) for _ in range(50)]
    # Introduce ties deliberately.
    for i in range(0, 50, 5):
        scores[i] = 42.0
    items = [{"id": ids[i], "score": scores[i]} for i in range(50)]
    expected = sorted(items, key=lambda x: (-x["score"], x["id"]))
    for size in [1, 2, 3, 7, 13, 100]:
        result, pages = walk_all(items, size)
        assert [x["id"] for x in result] == [x["id"] for x in expected], (size, result)
        assert len(result) == len(items)
    print("test_walk_all_mixed ok")


def test_no_duplicate_items():
    items = [{"id": f"id{i:03d}", "score": float(i % 4)} for i in range(20)]
    result, _ = walk_all(items, 4)
    ids = [x["id"] for x in result]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))
    assert len(ids) == len(items)
    print("test_no_duplicate_items ok")


def test_no_duplicate_items_across_pages_ties():
    # Every item has the same score; ensure each appears exactly once.
    items = [{"id": f"x{i:03d}", "score": 7.0} for i in range(30)]
    result, _ = walk_all(items, 5)
    ids = [x["id"] for x in result]
    assert sorted(ids) == sorted(x["id"] for x in items)
    assert len(ids) == 30
    print("test_no_duplicate_items_across_pages_ties ok")


def test_size_validation():
    for bad in [0, -1, -100]:
        try:

    print("test_size_validation ok")
